## Body

ROUND 2 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES (final round, C34).
Subject: pr:320
Head: fe67c7e26d89c3abbc18b5cd139f77714fba56c1
Answers: 01a1fe9e-a0cb-7480-9b8d-29ac008b5ec9

The added reads and renewal-debt set are bounded by the work they serve; no new timer, poll, task or process-launch site appears in the R2 production delta. The corrected retry wording now matches the changed implementation: successful F260 recovery is no longer repeated merely because the renewal audit append failed. No demonstrated normal-use resource-cost regression blocks this head. This cost verdict does not clear the independent correctness/security reviews, including their daemon-restart ordering question.

Verified cost:

| Path | Incremental work and rate |
|---|---|
| Lapse decision brake | After on_lapse's existing registry read and eligibility checks, native_receiver_renewed takes the global native mutex, does one additional registry.get, then one lease-map lookup under its mutex. The real store read is one schema PRAGMA plus one keyed SELECT and descriptor decoding, not one SQL statement or a process probe. The registry await is inside the shared native critical section. Identity matches PID, process start and native session; elapsed lease time is checked in memory. |
| Trigger scaling | One such brake call per eligible on_lapse invocation: live lapse events and outstanding-lapse decisions during startup/gap reconciliation. The 10-second completion-based cooldown bounds gap reconciles only. With U eligible outstanding seats, a gap scan adds U registry calls/lease lookups, hence 2U store statements, beyond the existing four-seek outstanding check per native seat. No cap on incoming heartbeat or live-event rates is implied. |
| Warm heartbeat | One extra owed-set mutex acquisition and contains lookup on every renewing heartbeat, even when the set is empty. Default lease 60s/divisor 3 recommends 20s between heartbeats, about 0.05 lookups/s per normally heartbeating seat; this is a client recommendation, not a server rate limit. |
| Ended lapse and failed audit | F260 recovery first performs its queue transaction/failed-history scan and H queued-outcome publications. Only complete success removes the lapsed mark and inserts one cloned seat ID into native_renewal_owed. While only the renewed append is failing, later heartbeats retry that spine write without repeating recover_held. Return-stage failure still leaves native_lapsed marked and can repeat the full return stage. A new expiry is a new lapse and can require another return. Success removes the debt entry. All this remains under the existing native mutex. |
| Debt-set bound | HashSet<SeatId>, not one entry per error, attempt, message or incarnation. Repeated failures for one seat do not grow its entry count. A successful receiver reconciliation retains only live native Copilot IDs from the same roster used to prune leases/lapse edges. There is no separate retention timer or hard numerical cap; closed/non-native entries can remain until a successful roster/prune pass. This is an entry-count bound, not a measured byte-allocation bound. |
| Existing reconciliation | The new retain pass runs on receiver reconciliation, not just auth-gap reconciliation. The existing drain has a nominal 5s configured tick plus lease-deadline wakes. With C live Copilot descriptors and O owed entries, the retain predicate can make up to O*C descriptor comparisons per pass. No additional roster query is introduced. Existing lease/lapse pruning already has this roster-search shape; R2 adds another pass and mutex section, not a new asymptotic class or scheduler. |

Sources: auth_recovery.rs:570-611,626-733; delivery/mod.rs:80-118,258-267,463-524,782-799,833-881,1000-1018; store/registry.rs:414-422; store/migrate.rs:242-247; daemon/lib.rs:846-877,1197-1198,1297-1299; core/config.rs:213.
